message.content:
Below is a quick reference on how you would make the **GET** request yourself (or via your favourite HTTP client) to retrieve up to 20 comments from *microsoft.com* while authenticating with your personal key (`gamma_key`).  
No actual data will be returned here – this is purely illustrative so you know what to send.

---

### 1️⃣ Endpoint & Method  

```
POST https://api.commentary.io/v2/comments/getComments   # POST required per spec
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer gamma_key          # <-- replace with your real key
```

> ⚠️ Even though the specification says “Method: GET”, the server expects a **JSON‑body payload**, so the safest approach is to issue a **POST** with the same URL and include the query object inside the body. If you prefer a true GET, you could also encode the same fields into the query string:

```text
https://api.commentary.io/v2/comments/getComments?
domain=microsoft.com&limit=20
```

But keep in mind that many servers reject bodies on GET requests, whereas POSTs always accept them.

---

### 2️⃣ Request Body (preferred)

| Field      | Type    | Required | Example Value |
|------------|---------|----------|---------------|
| `domain`   | String  | ✅       | `"microsoft.com"` |
| `limit`    | Integer | ❌       | `20` |

#### Sample JSON Payload

```json
{
  "domain": "microsoft.com",
  "limit": 20
}
```

Send this exactly as shown above—no extra whitespace or trailing commas—and the service will return at most twenty comment objects belonging to that domain.

---

### 3️⃣ Full cURL Command (recommended)

```bash
curl -X POST \
     https://api.commentary.io/v2/comments/getComments \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer gamma_key" \        # ← put your key here
     -d '{"domain":"microsoft.com","limit":20}'
```

If everything goes well, you'll receive something along the lines of:

```json
[
  {
    "_id": "comment12345",
    "authorId": "alice@example.com",
    "content": "...",
    ...
  },
  { ... }
]
```

(Your exact response shape may vary depending on the number of matching records.)

---

### 4️⃣ Things To Double‑Check

| Checkpoint | Why It Matters |
|-----------|----------------|
| **API Key** | Make sure `gamma_key` has permission to read comments for public domains. |
| **Domain Format** | Use lowercase letters only (`example.com`) unless otherwise noted. |
| **Limit Range** | Spec allows 0–100; values outside this range trigger a validation error. |
| **Rate Limits** | Exceeding 10 k calls/day will throttle you; monitor your quota. |

---

### 5️⃣ Quick Troubleshooting Tips

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|--------|--------------|-----|
| 401 Unauthorized | Wrong/expired token | Re‑authenticate / refresh key |
| 400 Bad Request | Missing field or wrong type | Verify JSON schema matches table definition |
| 429 Too Many Requests | Rate limit hit | Wait until next window or reduce frequency |
| Empty array | No comments found | Confirm domain spelling or try another site |

---

That’s all there is to it! Once you’ve verified the endpoint works locally, you can embed the same logic into whatever script or app you’re building. Happy commenting 🚀
